evidence_used.statement: Xinjiang cuisine combines Chinese, Central Asian and Middle Eastern cooking traditions; it is predominantly halal, featuring lamb, cumin/chili seasoning, nang flatbread, noodles and pilaf.
Classic Xinjiang dishes commonly shared with visitors include da pan ji (big-plate chicken), hand-pulled noodles, and naan/nang flatbread.
Kashgar's local food scene features smoked meat, pomegranates, milk tea and spiced bread, with seasonings such as cumin, chili, cinnamon, garlic and sesame.
According to Lonely Planet, China operates the world's largest high-speed rail network connecting more than 500 cities, with trains reaching up to about 350 km/h.
Travel guides note that everyday life in Chinese cities is largely cashless, with WeChat Pay and Alipay widely used for metro fares, street food and other daily transactions.
Lonely Planet describes Beijing hutong districts around Gulou and the Lama Temple as places where visitors encounter historic alleyway life on a human scale.
